title: CRLA/316/2002 of MOHABATH SINGH Vs STATE

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No.316 of 2002
Mohabath Singh ... Appellant
vs.
State of Uttarakhand ... Respondent
Mr. Miland Raj, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Deepak Tiwari, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. Suhail Ahmad Siddiqui, A.G.A. for the State.
Hon'ble U. C. Dhyani, J. (Oral)
1. PW1 Saahab Singh wrote a complaint (Ex.Ka-1) to the
Incharge Kotwali, Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar on
09.12.1998, which was registered as case crime no.1376/1998 at
Police Station Rudrapur for the offences punishable under
Sections 302 / 307 IPC. Mohabath Singh (appellant herein),
Amarjeet Singh, Malook Singh and Kuldeep Singh were named in
the FIR.
2. Investigation began on the basis of said first information
report. After investigation of the case, a charge-sheet (Ex.Ka-5)
was submitted against the accused persons, namely, Mohabath
Singh (appellant), Amarjeet Singh, Malook Singh and Kuldeep
Singh for the offences punishable under Sections 302 / 307 IPC.
The case was committed to the Court of Sessions. When the trial
began and prosecution opened it's case, charges against
Mohabath Singh (appellant-accused), Amarjeet Singh, Malook
Singh and Kuldeep Singh were framed for the offences
punishable under Section 302 IPC read with Section 34 IPC and
Section 307 IPC read with Section 34 IPC.
3. PW1 Saahab Singh, PW2 Smt. Mahendra Kaur, PW3
Harbhajan Singh, PW4 Dr. M. S. Sharma, PW5 Vinod Kumar

-2-
Sharma, PW6 K. C. Pundir, PW7 Vikram Singh and PW8
Virendra Singh Raghav were examined on behalf of the
prosecution. Incriminating evidence was put to the accused
persons under Section 313 Cr.P.C., in reply to which they said
that they were falsely implicated in the case. No evidence was
given in defence.
4. After conclusion of the trial, learned Sessions Judge,
District Udham Singh Nagar, vide judgment and order dated
18.11.2002, exonerated the accused persons for the charges
under Sections 302/34 IPC & 307/34 IPC. Accused-appellant
was, however, found guilty and was convicted of the offence
punishable under Section 304-A IPC. He was directed to
undergo rigorous imprisonment for 2 years. Aggrieved against
the same, the present criminal appeal was preferred by the
appellant.

5. PW1, in his examination-in-chief, supported the
prosecution story. He said that the incident took place on
09.12.1998 at about 11:30 AM. He said that he alongwith his
mother (PW2) was present at Pandit's shop near Kichha by-pass
road. Sukhvinder Singh came from the side of Rudrapur. He
was talking to PW1 and PW2. Accused-appellant and co-accused
persons wanted to forcibly occupy the land of PW1. A truck
bearing registration no.UP14 7435, which was being driven by
appellant-Mohabath Singh (and other accused were sitting inside
the truck), came from the side of Kichha. Other accused persons
exhorted the appellant to kill PW1, PW2 and the victim
(Sukhvinder Singh). Accused-appellant was about to kill them.
PW1 and PW2 withdrew themselves, but the victim Sukhvinder
Singh could not alight himself from the scooter. The appellant
hit and crushed Sukhvinder Singh beneath the truck. The

-3-
incident was witnessed by Harbhajan Singh and Rajwant Singh.
Accused-appellant and other accused persons fled away towards
the fields. PW1 and PW2 went to the Government Hospital,
Rudrapur. Sukhvinder Singh could not be saved and he
succumbed to his injuries. Complaint (Ex.Ka-1) was written with
the assistance of Harbhajan Singh. PW1 was cross-examined at
length, but nothing adverse came in his statement, so as to
suggest that PW1's testimony should be treated with suspicion.
6. PW2 Smt. Mahendra Kaur also supported the prosecution
story and corroborated the statement of PW1. She also said that
PW1, Rajwant Singh and Harbhajan Singh chased the accused
persons, but one of them threatened with dire consequences by
firing pistol in the air. PW2 was also cross-examined by the
defence counsel but nothing adverse came in her statement so as
to disbelieve her testimony.
7. PW3 Harbhajan Singh was also an eyewitness of the
incident, who supported the testimony of PW1 and PW2. PW4
Dr. M. S. Sharma, Medical Officer conducted the postmortem on
the dead body of the deceased on 10.12.1998 and proved the
postmortem report (Ex.Ka-2). PW4 opined that the ante-mortem
injuries sustained by the deceased could have been inflicted on
09.12.1998 at 11:00 AM. It was possible that the ante-mortem
injuries were sustained by collision with a heavy vehicle.'
8. PW5 was the Investigating Officer of the case. He
conducted the investigation of the case at some length.
Remaining part of the investigation was conducted by PW6
Inspector K. C. Pundir, who concluded the same by filing charge-sheet (Ex.Ka-5).

-4-
9. PW7 was a formal witness, who proved the chick FIR
(Ex.Ka-6), the entry of the same in the G.D. (Ex.Ka-7) and other
related papers.
10. The testimony of PW1, PW2 and PW3 inspired confidence.
The oral testimony of PW1, PW2 & PW3 was further
corroborated by PW4 (medical evidence). The prosecution story
was further supported by the peripheral evidence of PW5, PW6,
PW7 & PW8. It is proved beyond reasonable doubt that on the
date and time of the incident, accused-appellant drove the truck
rashly and negligently, due to which the truck crushed the victim
resulting into his death. Had the accused-appellant intention to
commit the murder of Sukhvinder Singh, PW1 & PW2, he would
not have spared PW1 and PW2 and also dashed them with his
truck. It, therefore, transpires that he had no intention to kill the
victim, but he was definitely driving truck rashly and negligently,
which cost the life of Sukhvinder Singh. The trial court was
correct in exonerating the appellant and other accused of the
charges under Sections 302 / 307 IPC and convicting the
appellant under Section 304-A IPC.
11. Learned trial court discussed and appreciated the
prosecution evidence correctly. Learned trial court, therefore,
committed no mistake in holding that the prosecution was able to
prove it's case under Section 304-A IPC against the accused-appellant beyond a shadow of reasonable doubt. This Court also
assessed the prosecution evidence independently to come to the
conclusion that the trial court has rightly held the appellant
guilty and convicted him for the offence punishable under
Section 304-A IPC, in as much as there is nothing on record to
disbelieve the evidence of PW1, PW2 and PW3. The evidence of
these eye-witnesses cannot be disregarded, minor discrepancies

-5-
in their testimony notwithstanding. The appellant was driving
the truck rashly and negligently, he proceeded towards the
victim, who could not alight from the scooter and therefore the
appellant dashed his truck with the victim, resulting in his
(Sukhvinder Singh's) death. No interference is, thus, called for in
the impugned judgment and order. The conviction of the
accused-appellant is hereby affirmed.
12. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the
appellant remained in jail for two months twice. He prayed that a
lenient view be taken against the appellant and the sentence
awarded to him be reduced in as much as he is ready to deposit
fine before the court below.

13. Taking into account the whole conspectus of things, it looks
proper if the period of sentence is reduced and the appellant is
directed to pay a fine, which should be given to the next of kin of
the victim as compensation.
14. The impugned judgment and order is, therefore, modified
to the extent that the accused-appellant shall undergo rigorous
imprisonment for a period of one year alongwith a fine of
Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand only). In default of
payment of fine, he shall further undergo Simple Imprisonment
for six months. If the amount of fine is recovered from the
appellant, then the same shall be awarded as compensation
under Section 357 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 to the
next of kin of the victim.
15. Criminal appeal preferred by the accused-appellant is,
therefore, dismissed with the above observations and
modification in the sentence. The accused-appellant is on bail.

-6-
His bail is cancelled. He is directed to surrender before the Court
concerned forthwith to serve out the sentence awarded to him by
this Court.
16. Let a copy of this judgment alongwith the lower court
record be sent to the court below for ensuring compliance as
above.
 (U. C. Dhyani, J.)
Dated 29th October, 2013 Rawat
